title: Chrome proportion shrink-only baseline — tempdoc 697
description: Schema for governance/ui-proportion-baseline.v1.json. Registers persistent-chrome elements (per ui-shot step) whose rendered height must not GROW beyond a recorded ceiling. Shrinking is always allowed. Mirrors ui-a11y-baseline.schema.json's shape (draft-07, additionalProperties: false).

constraintKinds.description: Prose summary of the constraint vocabulary an element may declare.

occlusionNote.description: Prose record of the measured defects the overlap/floor constraints were added for, including the honest residual.

rolesNote.description: Prose record of what a ROLE is, why bounds are in content units, and the anti-vacuity rule role-bound rows inherit.

roles.description: Tempdoc 816 §3/§4a.1 — the FUNCTIONAL role vocabulary. A role declares inline-axis bounds in CONTENT units (`ch`), resolved at measure time against the bound element's OWN rendered font (ui_measure.py's per-element `chPx`), so a role means the same number of characters on 11px chrome and a 16px banner. Element rows reference a role via `inlineSizeRole` instead of repeating numbers. Logical (flow-relative) naming is deliberate (§2c): role bounds follow text flow, while the physical constraint kinds (minWidthPx/maxHeightPx/…) keep their physical names because occlusion and viewport-fit are physical facts.

why.description: The FUNCTION that produces the bound. §3: a bound that cannot cite a function does not belong in the register.

minInlineSizeCh.description: Functional minimum in `ch`. A role-bound row measuring below this (minus tolerancePx) is UNDER_MEASURE.

maxInlineSizeCh.description: Functional maximum in `ch` (the reading MEASURE, the industry name — §4b). A role-bound row measuring above this (plus tolerancePx) is OVER_MEASURE.

token.description: The CSS custom property in modules/ui-web/src/styles/tokens.css that RENDERS this role's maximum. The gate asserts the token's value equals `<maxInlineSizeCh>ch` — one authority renders AND judges (§4a.3, the catalog-verbatim pattern). Omit for a role with no rendered token.

documentational.description: True for a role declared for vocabulary completeness that no element row references yet (e.g. `pane`, whose members are already covered physically by minWidthPx/minShareOfSelector rows). A documentational role is never resolved, so it needs no bound; referencing one from a row is an error.

tolerancePx.description: Default growth tolerance in px, applied when a step/element does not override it. A measured height is a violation only when it exceeds maxHeightPx + tolerancePx.

steps.description: Per-ui-shot-step registration of tracked chrome elements. An empty array is valid — no elements are tracked yet (placeholder state; heights are filled in later via regen_proportion_baseline.py).

uiShotStep.description: The jsharness ui-shot step name this registration is captured under.

$comment.description: Why this step's rows exist / what state they are measured in — the reasoning that would otherwise live only in a commit message.

tolerancePx.description: Optional per-step override of the top-level tolerancePx.

maxScrollableRegions.description: Tempdoc 814 D3/D7.2 — one-scroll-region-per-surface. When set, the gate asserts geometry.scrollableCount (ui_measure.py's shadow-piercing scrollable-element walk) is <= this value.

minScrollableRegions.description: Closure-audit finding C — the anti-vacuity FLOOR paired with maxScrollableRegions. A ceiling alone passes trivially on a capture with zero scrollers, so a step whose state is supposed to overflow declares this floor; the pair (1/1) is what makes the one-scroller rule witness a real scroller. A scrollableCount below this is a NO_SCROLLER violation.

statusFactsSingleton.description: Tempdoc 814 D5/D7.3 — when true, the gate asserts every phrase in governance/status-facts.v1.json renders at most its registered maxPersistentRenders times in this step's captured DOM text (measure.json's statusFacts probe).

absentSelectors.description: Tempdoc 814 D7.2 — selectors that must NOT be present in the captured geometry (e.g. the run-spine on a single-turn conversation). A present selector is a PRESENT_BUT_SHOULD_BE_ABSENT violation. Unioned into ui_measure.py's geometry probe like `selector`/`mustNotOverlapSelector`.

requiredSelectors.description: Tempdoc 814 D7.2 — absentSelectors' positive twin (the spine PAIR): selectors that MUST be present in the captured geometry (e.g. the run-spine on a multi-turn agent run). An absent selector is a MISSING_REQUIRED violation. Declared on the STEP, not as an element row, because the assertion is presence itself — an element row with no size constraint is an error by design. Unioned into ui_measure.py's geometry probe.

nonScrollableSelectors.description: Tempdoc 814 D8 — selectors that must be PRESENT and must NOT be scrollers: D3's one-scroller rule addressed at a NAMED element. maxScrollableRegions bounds the surface TOTAL and structurally cannot say which element may scroll (a capture where .conversation stopped scrolling and the evidence rail started still counts 1). Judged off the element's own geometry.elements[sel].scrollable flag, computed by ui_measure.py with the same overflow+delta predicate that builds scrollableRegions, so this is 'absent from scrollableRegions' addressed by the registered selector rather than by that walk's truncated description string. A missing selector is an IS_SCROLLER violation too (a must-not-scroll assertion on an element that never mounted asserts nothing). Unioned into ui_measure.py's geometry probe.

forbiddenVisibleText.description: Tempdoc 814 D5 (review pass) — literal phrases that must not render VISIBLY in this step's capture; count > 0 is a FORBIDDEN_TEXT_VISIBLE violation. Counted by the same visibility-filtered statusFacts probe the status-facts register feeds, but STEP-scoped with a ceiling of 0. Its case: the chip-yield duplication is cross-wording (banner 'Semantic search degraded.' vs. chip 'Service degraded'), which a same-phrase counter cannot witness — what a capture CAN decide is that the banner-owning surface does not also show the chip's wording.

items.description: An element declares at least one geometric constraint; the gate reports an element with none as an ERROR rather than a silent pass.

selector.description: Shadow-piercing CSS selector (resolved via ui_measure.py's deepQuery), e.g. 'jf-rail'.

maxHeightPx.description: Recorded rendered-height ceiling in px. A measured height above maxHeightPx + tolerancePx is a growth violation.

minHeightPx.description: Tempdoc 814 (review pass) — the ceiling's anti-vacuity FLOOR companion. A maxHeightPx alone is satisfied by an element that COLLAPSED (the Detailed banner's 176px ceiling passes at 34px, exactly when Detailed expansion regressed to the collapsed pill), so a band registered because it EXPANDS declares both bounds. A measured height below minHeightPx - tolerancePx is an UNDER_MIN_HEIGHT violation.

minWidthPx.description: Rendered-width FLOOR in px for primary content that chrome must not starve. A measured width below minWidthPx - tolerancePx is a starvation violation.

maxWidthPx.description: Tempdoc 816 — minWidthPx's symmetric CEILING: the rendered width must not exceed this (plus tolerancePx). The physical-family twin, for an element whose function-derived bound is its CONTAINER rather than a line length (a control row is intrinsic-width; §3's `control-row` max is `fit-content`, which is not expressible in `ch`). Only meaningful on a step with a pinned viewport, exactly like maxHeightPx.

inlineSizeRole.description: Tempdoc 816 §4a.2 — bind this element to a `roles` entry instead of repeating numbers. The gate resolves the role's ch bounds against the element's OWN captured `chPx`. ANTI-VACUITY: a ceiling alone would pass on a collapsed/failed render, so a role-bound row must also have a floor — either the role's `minInlineSizeCh` or the row's own `minWidthPx`; a row with neither is an ERROR.

mustNotOverlapSelector.description: A second registered selector whose rect this element's rect must not intersect (by more than tolerancePx on both axes). Expresses occlusion, which no per-element size budget can.

minShareOfSelector.description: Tempdoc 814 D1/D7.1 — the owner-of-the-sum share assertion: this element's rect.h divided by a second registered selector's rect.h must be >= floor. Expresses 'primary content owns the remainder', which no absolute px ceiling/floor can.

selector.description: The denominator element's selector (e.g. the surface host, 'jf-unified-chat-view').

floor.description: Minimum acceptable share (0-1) of the denominator's height this element's height must occupy.

maxBottomPx.description: Tempdoc 814 D6/D7.2 (the F5 close) — rect.y + rect.h must not exceed this value + tolerancePx, i.e. the element's bottom edge must stay within a viewport of this height.
